slots.workflow-matrix/title: Release decisions depend on validated measures, controls, runbooks, and recovery
slots.workflow-matrix/matrix-takeaway/text: Targets follow an agreed baseline; the measures above are candidate definitions, not claimed benefits.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-0: Teams re-enter customer and case details across channels. Incomplete requests create clarification loops and inconsistent handoffs. Discovery produces validated baseline and sampling notes.

Capture required information once, validate it at entry and route exceptions to a named owner. Retain human review where judgment or policy requires it. Target values require agreed definitions and validated baseline data.
Pilot measures include intake completeness, manual handoffs, decision latency, rework, and recoverability.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-1: Candidate targets are manual handoffs from the assumed 22% toward 12%, incomplete intake from the assumed 14% toward 7%, and at least 95% traceability to an owner and timestamp.

Assemble a traceable case record through managed interfaces. Show source provenance, missing evidence and reconciliation status before the case advances. The discovery baseline is assumed, not independently validated.
Preparation time; missing evidence; duplicate records; reconciliation exceptions
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-2: Work queues hide dependency and approval status. Escalations rely on messages, and the rationale for decisions can be difficult to recover. Do not declare success from activity completion alone.
Make state, ownership and approval rules explicit. Route exceptions by reason, capture decision rationale and retain an auditable record of human approvals.
Queue age; approval time; exception volume; reopened cases; audit completeness
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-3: Proceed to pilot only after owners accept test evidence, critical control findings are resolved, operations can run the runbooks, and rollback is rehearsed.

Publish validated events and managed APIs. Monitor end-to-end completion, expose failed handoffs and provide controlled retry, rollback and recovery procedures. The candidate targets are directional hypotheses, not performance commitments.
Proceed to expansion only when validated baseline and pilot data support the decision.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-4: It also produces a journey and ownership map, interface and dependency register, prioritized thin-release backlog, and agreed control and acceptance checklist.
Create a shared measurement cadence with agreed definitions and owners. Use observed outcomes to prioritize the backlog, assess controls and select the next wave.
If evidence is weak or conditions change, adjust scope and retain the existing service.
slots.slide/takeaway: Pilot evidence—not activity completion—determines whether to proceed, adjust, or hold.
